clue.text: Married, keeping promise at altar with or without partner

indicators.note: the word for married holds the other pieces within it, as if keeping them

parts.note: to wed is to marry; the past tense gives the shell
I DO is the vow spoken at a wedding

explanation.surface: A description of someone married, keeping their vow, perhaps with or without a spouse beside them.
explanation.walkthrough: W is the standard abbreviation for with; 'or' is a link, leaving 'without partner' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A widowed person has lost their spouse to death and so is left alone, without a husband or wife.

clue.text: Refuse cider, essentially hammered

parts.note: refuse as a noun is rubbish, waste

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so only the central letter of cider is used

parts.note: the central letter of the word cider is its essence

explanation.surface: Someone turns down cider, being already very drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' reads as the verb to decline, but it is the noun meaning rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are slang adjectives for being very drunk.

clue.text: Doctor sorry in Wilts

parts.note: oops is the little apology you say after a blunder

explanation.surface: A doctor apologises somewhere in Wiltshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Wilts is the usual short form of Wiltshire, an English county, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To wilt is to sag or hang limply, as a flower does without water.

clue.text: Seal in lake perhaps? Verification to follow

indicators.note: says the verification piece comes after the lake piece

parts.note: a lake is one example of a body of water
proof is evidence that verifies a claim

explanation.surface: A seal is spotted in a lake, with confirmation to come later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seal' looks like the animal swimming in the lake; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To waterproof something is to seal it so that no moisture can get through.

clue.text: Avoid scam

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a verb, to evade or sidestep
second meaning: a noun, a crafty trick or swindle

explanation.walkthrough: Two separate senses of one short word, the verb and the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to dodge out of the way and, informally, a dishonest racket.

clue.text: Test rejected quantity of chemical — acid emerged

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the hidden letters are read backwards
a quantity of the words is only a portion of them, so the answer lies inside

explanation.surface: A lab test is thrown out after a dose of chemical produced acid.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical is a physical examination, a check-up testing someone's health.

clue.text: Hand one restores to health with these?

definitions.text: Hand one restores to health with these?

parts.note: a hand is a worker, a man employed on a farm or ship
the Roman numeral for one
to cure is to make well again

explanation.surface: Asks whether these treatments are what bring a hand back to good condition.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes the treatment itself, which restores a hand to looking its best.
explanation.definitionFit: Manicures are cosmetic treatments for the hands and fingernails.

clue.text: Blast! … almost late rising

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the letters are read from bottom to top
almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: tardy means late

explanation.surface: Someone curses at nearly being late getting up.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild exclamations of annoyance.

clue.text: Liberal, one seen in mass meeting?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: broad-minded or wide-ranging in tastes
second meaning: a member of the Roman church, attending Mass

explanation.walkthrough: A 'mass meeting' sounds like a big rally, but the second sense is someone at a church Mass.
explanation.definitionFit: Lower-case the word means universal or broad in sympathies; capitalised it names a member of the Roman church.

clue.text: Fifty grand to imprison young rascal, it's staggering

indicators.note: the two outer letters lock the rascal up between them

parts.note: an urchin is a mischievous child

explanation.surface: Paying fifty thousand to lock up a young rogue is astonishing.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the Roman numeral for fifty and G is slang for a grand. 'Staggering' looks like 'astonishing'; it means reeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Lurching and staggering both describe moving unsteadily with sudden jerks.

clue.text: Left by end of fireworks display

indicators.note: places the piece for left beside the final letter
the last letter of fireworks is taken

parts.note: the last letter of fireworks
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Someone is left standing at the finish of a fireworks show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Display' looks like the fireworks show itself; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To sport something is to wear or show it off proudly.

clue.text: Scholar shed tears from time to time in northern city

parts.note: a don is a university teacher
to cast is to shed, as a snake casts its skin

indicators.note: only now and then, so every other letter of tears is taken

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of tears

explanation.surface: An academic weeps every now and then in a city in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shed tears' reads as weeping; the two words split into separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Doncaster is a city in South Yorkshire, in the north of England.

clue.text: Encounter abrupt professional upsetting niece

indicators.note: abrupt means cut short, so the last letter is removed

parts.note: an expert is a skilled professional

indicators.note: upsetting the niece knocks her letters into a new order

parts.note: the five letters of niece, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An encounter with a curt professional who distresses a young relative.
explanation.definitionFit: To experience something is to meet with it or undergo it, as a verb.

clue.text: United leaving trap for winger

indicators.note: the letter for United departs from the word

parts.note: trap is slang for mouth, as in 'shut your trap'

explanation.surface: A football tale: United quit a trap set for their wide player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United' and 'winger' suggest football; a winger here is anything with wings.
explanation.definitionFit: A moth is a winged insect, so playfully a creature that flies on wings.

clue.text: Shirking one's duty, a capital offence?

definitions.meaning: duty here is a levy owed to the state, so the dodging is of payments
capital here means money, so the crime concerns cash rather than execution

explanation.walkthrough: 'Duty' suggests obligation and 'capital offence' a crime punishable by death; both are about money.
explanation.definitionFit: Illegally avoiding paying what the revenue is owed is a financial crime.

clue.text: Keeping tax cuts agitated senior rep

indicators.note: the tax cuts into the jumbled letters, sitting inside them
agitated letters are stirred up into a new order

parts.note: the nine letters of senior rep, to be rearranged
VAT is value added tax, the British sales tax

explanation.surface: Holding onto tax reductions has upset a senior sales representative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeping' looks like part of the surface verb; it is a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: Preservation is the act of keeping something safe or maintaining it.

clue.text: Building reportedly hit on top at first? Certainly top's missing

indicators.note: signals a word heard rather than spelt, giving only its sound

parts.note: struck means hit

indicators.note: only the opening letter of top is taken

parts.note: the opening letter of the word top

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter, here dropped

parts.note: sure means certainly, as a reply

explanation.surface: A building said to have been struck on its roof first, with its roof surely gone.
explanation.walkthrough: The sound of struck supplies the opening letters, spelt without the K.
explanation.definitionFit: A structure is anything built, such as an edifice or construction.

clue.text: Assumed one's permitted to keep parking inside

indicators.note: the outer letters hold the parking letter
confirms the parking letter sits within

parts.note: one's read as one is, which from a speaker becomes I'm
licit means lawful, allowed

explanation.surface: Someone takes for granted they may park in an inside spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Something implicit is understood or taken for granted without being stated.

clue.text: Stretch out scandal involving Tesla boss?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a verb, to make longer
second meaning, whimsical: a scandal about Elon Musk would be named in the Watergate style

explanation.surface: Wonders whether a scandal involving the head of Tesla will drag on.
explanation.walkthrough: Scandals take the suffix -gate after Watergate, so one about Elon Musk, who runs Tesla, would be this word.
explanation.definitionFit: To elongate is to lengthen, to make longer.

clue.text: Load menu liberally, admitting PM for the most part's short of food

indicators.note: the jumbled letters let the PM piece in
freely and without restraint, so the letters are loosely rearranged

parts.note: these letters are reworked

indicators.note: most of the name, so the last letter goes

parts.note: Rishi Sunak was the British Prime Minister

explanation.surface: A greedy diner piles on the dishes, yet admits the Prime Minister is mostly underfed.
explanation.walkthrough: Rishi Sunak was the UK Prime Minister from 2022 to 2024.
explanation.definitionFit: Being malnourished means lacking proper nutrition, from too little to eat.

clue.text: One with swollen head say gets lift wanting hospital

parts.note: eg means for example, which is what say means here

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the hospital letter is missing

parts.note: to hoist is to lift

explanation.surface: A head injury, perhaps, needing a lift but no longer needing hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swollen head' suggests injury; it means conceit.
explanation.definitionFit: An egoist is self-centred and conceited, figuratively bigheaded.

clue.text: Called time on daughter taking Ecstasy

indicators.note: in a down clue, on places the time word above the rest
the daughter takes the drug letter onto herself ahead of her

parts.note: a term is a fixed period of time

explanation.surface: Someone called time on their daughter for taking drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: E is the usual abbreviation for the drug Ecstasy.
explanation.definitionFit: Termed and called both mean named or described as.

clue.text: Offer fix, go up a size to start with

indicators.text: go up a size to start with
indicators.note: clothes go up from medium to large, so the opening medium letter becomes the large one

parts.note: to mend is to fix

explanation.surface: Advice on altering clothes: offer a fix, going up one size first.
explanation.walkthrough: M and L are clothing sizes, medium and large.
explanation.definitionFit: To lend can mean to give or offer, as in lending support or a hand.

clue.text: Outlook following a hint about temperature, it's below 90 degrees

indicators.note: the outlook piece comes after the others

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the hint goes around the temperature letter

parts.note: a cue is a prompt or hint
an angle is a point of view, an outlook

explanation.surface: A weather forecast hinting that the temperature will fall below ninety degrees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Temperature' and '90 degrees' suggest weather; the degrees are those of an angle.
explanation.definitionFit: An acute angle is any angle less than a right angle.

clue.text: Ferried small child over sea miles away

indicators.note: in a down clue over places the child piece on top

parts.note: a tot is a toddler

indicators.note: the miles letter goes away from the sea word

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: A little child was carried across the sea for miles.
explanation.definitionFit: To tote is to carry or transport, as goods or passengers.

clue.text: Ultimately drives taxi to make a crust

indicators.note: the final letter of drives is taken

parts.note: the final letter of drives
a cab is a taxi

explanation.surface: Someone ends up driving a taxi to earn a living.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make a crust' is British slang for earning a living; here crust is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A scab is the hard crust that forms over a healing wound.

clue.text: Head of church (non-clerical) has date to practise service here?

indicators.note: only the first letter of church is used

parts.note: the opening letter of church
lay people are those not ordained as clergy
to court someone is to date them

explanation.surface: A vicar's lay assistant is booked to rehearse a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' looks ecclesiastical after church and clerical; it is the tennis serve.
explanation.definitionFit: A clay court is a tennis surface, where players practise their serves.

clue.text: Language of fool wasting time with maiden

indicators.note: the time letter is used up and lost from the word

parts.note: an idiot is a fool

explanation.surface: Talk from a fool frittering away time with a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: M for maiden is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a maiden over.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is a form of expression, the characteristic language of a people or group.

clue.text: Mike tucking into triple shake

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the other word, as food goes into a mouth

parts.note: treble means threefold
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Mike eagerly eats a triple-sized milkshake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tucking into' and 'shake' suggest a man eating; shake is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To tremble is to shake or quiver, as from cold or fear.

clue.text: Gifted mafia boss pontificated after gold goes missing

indicators.note: the speech piece comes after the boss piece

parts.note: a don is a Mafia chief

indicators.note: the gold letters are lost from the word

parts.note: to orate is to speak pompously
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A gifted crime lord preached after the gold disappeared.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is heraldic gold. 'Gifted' looks like 'talented'; it is the verb in the past tense.
explanation.definitionFit: Donated and gifted both mean given away freely.
